final_proof:
Let \(S_a=\{i\in I:x_a(i)\ne0\}\), and put
\[
J=\bigcup_{a=1}^m S_a.
\]
Each \(S_a\) is countable, and this is a finite union, so \(J\) is countable. Hence there is an injection \(\phi:J\to\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\). For each \(a\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define a sequence \(y_a=(y_{a,n})_{n\ge0}\) by
\[
y_{a,n}=\begin{cases}
x_a(i),&\text{if }n=\phi(i)\text{ for some }i\in J,\\
0,&\text{if }n\notin\phi(J).
\end{cases}
\]
This is well-defined because \(\phi\) is injective.

We first record why this reindexing preserves all sums in question. The generalized sum of a nonnegative family \((c_i)_{i\in I}\) is the limit of the net
\[
F\longmapsto \sum_{i\in F}c_i
\]
over the finite subsets \(F\) of \(I\), ordered by inclusion. If \(c_i=0\) outside \(J\), define
\[
J_N=\{i\in J:\phi(i)\le N\}\qquad(N\ge0).
\]
Every \(J_N\) is finite. Moreover, for every finite \(F\subseteq I\), the set \(F\cap J\) is contained in \(J_N\) for all sufficiently large \(N\), and the terms indexed outside \(J\) are zero. Thus, whenever the generalized sum converges,
\[
\sum_{i\in I}c_i
=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{i\in J_N}c_i
=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\widetilde c_n,
\]
where \(\widetilde c_{\phi(i)}=c_i\) for \(i\in J\) and \(\widetilde c_n=0\) outside \(\phi(J)\).

Apply this observation with \(c_i=x_a(i)^2\). By the defining property of \(A\), its generalized sum is finite. It follows that
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}y_{a,n}^2
=\sum_{i\in I}x_a(i)^2<\infty.
\]
Thus \(y_a\in\ell^2\) for every \(a\).

Now fix \(a,b\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). The family \(((x_a(i)-x_b(i))^2)_{i\in I}\) vanishes outside \(J\). Its net of finite partial sums is increasing and bounded, since for every finite \(F\subseteq I\),
\[
\sum_{i\in F}(x_a(i)-x_b(i))^2
\le 2\sum_{i\in F}x_a(i)^2+2\sum_{i\in F}x_b(i)^2
\le 2\sum_{i\in I}x_a(i)^2+2\sum_{i\in I}x_b(i)^2.
\]
It therefore converges to the supremum of its finite partial sums. Applying the reindexing observation to this family gives
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(y_{a,n}-y_{b,n})^2
=\sum_{i\in I}(x_a(i)-x_b(i))^2.
\]
Taking nonnegative square roots yields
\[
d_{\ell^2}(y_a,y_b)=d_2(x_a,x_b).
\]

Finally, if \(x_a=x_b\), the definition immediately gives \(y_a=y_b\). Conversely, if \(y_a=y_b\), then for every \(i\in J\), comparison at coordinate \(\phi(i)\) gives \(x_a(i)=x_b(i)\); for \(i\notin J\), both values are zero by the definition of \(J\). Hence \(x_a=x_b\). Therefore
\[
y_a\ne y_b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x_a\ne x_b,
\]
and both required conclusions hold for all \(a,b\in[1,m]\).
